nodes.label: More access, more boundary crossing
nodes.rationale: Moving from Closed/Task to Open access drops task success 90%->72% and safe success 74%->54%, while boundary violation rises 20%->36%. 50 valid of 60 planned runs per level.

nodes.label: Boundary crossing kinds by model
nodes.rationale: Write events dominate out-of-scope incidents. Gemma 4 31B has 23 events (10 executed, only model with Execute events); Claude Opus 5.5 has just 1 list event.

nodes.label: Fig 08: Capability vs boundary discipline
nodes.rationale: Claude Opus 5.5 has lowest violation rate (~7%) at ~73% success; Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol ~93% success/~13% violations; Gemma 4 31B worst (~47%); GPT-6 Luna lowest success (~47%). Capability and discipline are largely independent.

nodes.rationale: GPT-6.1 Sol (~$0.31, 0.89) and Claude Sonnet 5.5 (~$0.47, 0.88) top score at moderate cost; GPT-6 Astra most expensive (~$1.7, 0.80); GPT-6 Luna cheapest (~$0.011) but lowest score (0.33). Higher spend does not guarantee higher score.
